_read_me: RIG-135 ratchet inventory for scripts/check-spawn-guard.js. class 'debt' = must route through rig/lib/spawn-guarded.js once it exists (matches a wrong-kill or ungrouped-timeout pattern the ticket's survey classifies as a real orphan-risk). class 'allowlisted' = individually verified short-lived/non-forking utility spawn, safe to stay outside the helper indefinitely, with rationale. class 'separate-follow-up' = real descendant-orphan risk confirmed, but the fix is subsystem-specific (Bun's own spawn API lacks the negative-pid group-kill primitive the Node-shaped helper relies on, or an intentional daemon/Chromium/Xvfb/device lifecycle needs its own reap contract) and needs separately owned design rather than a mechanical migration to the current helper shape. class 'pending-triage' = mechanically detected but NOT yet individually verified either way; do not read presence on this list as a safety claim. Never delete an entry silently -- reclassify with a reason.

sites.ref: brain doctor is guarded; the remaining timeout is a fixed one-shot gitleaks version/file scan
execSync runs a short one-shot python correctness probe via EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS; not a forking runtime
execSync runs a short one-shot python robustness probe; not a forking runtime
execSync("git remote get-url origin", {timeout: 5000}) -- fixed one-shot git command, does not fork
runCommand() wrapper is only ever called with git/gh/glab/rig-config -- all fixed one-shot CLIs, none are forking runtimes

verified 2026-08-26: gitState() runs a fixed 'git rev-list' (non-forking); scanBeforeActivation() runs configured.command, but that value is restricted to the hardcoded SCANNERS array (gitleaks or trufflehog only, resolved via PATH) -- not user/caller-configurable, and both are single-process Go CLI scanners with no evidence of forking children

verified 2026-08-26: git() helper always spawns a fixed 'git' executable with caller-supplied git-subcommand args (rev-parse/worktree/add/diff) -- git does not fork long-lived descendants for these subcommands. Also currently has zero callers in the repo (WorktreeManager is unused/dead code); re-verify if/when it gets wired up

verified 2026-08-26: the only real spawn+timeout is Bun.spawnSync([chromePath, '--version'], {timeout}) -- a one-shot Chromium version probe that exits immediately without spawning renderer/GPU children. The other flagged line is a Playwright launchPersistentContext({timeout}) option, a launch-handshake deadline, not a raw spawn/kill call -- mechanical-scan false positive. The long-lived multi-process Chromium browser is launched and torn down entirely through Playwright's own chromium.launch()/browser.close(), outside child_process/Bun.spawn and outside this ticket's scope

verified 2026-08-26: cp.spawnSync('git', ['rev-parse','--show-toplevel'], {timeout:2000}) -- the exact Category E example (git rev-parse) the ticket itself names as low-risk; no kill call, non-forking
verified 2026-08-26: cp.spawnSync('git', ['rev-parse','--show-toplevel'], {timeout:2000}) inside auth/state-file resolution; non-forking, falls back to process.cwd() on failure
verified 2026-08-26: two Bun.spawnSync(['git', ...], {timeout:2000}) calls (getGitRoot/getRemoteSlug), both fixed non-forking git reads with safe fallbacks on timeout

verified 2026-08-26: the only real spawn+timeout is a Windows-only Bun.spawnSync(['tasklist', ...], {timeout:3000}) liveness probe, non-forking. safeKill()/process.kill(pid,0) in this file are generic single-pid primitives consumed by other, separately tracked files, not spawn sites of their own

verified 2026-08-26: execFileSync('node', ['--version'], {timeout:2000}) is a one-shot interpreter-presence probe, non-forking. This file only resolves a path; the actual sidecar subprocess it points at is launched and killed elsewhere (security-sidecar-client.ts, already tracked as a separate debt site)

verified 2026-08-26: execSync('osascript -e ...', {timeout:3000}) activates one of a fixed 5-item enumerated app-name list (not caller-controlled), non-forking, failures caught per-iteration. Other 'timeout' occurrences in this file are Playwright in-browser action timeouts, not process spawns -- mechanical-scan false positives

verified 2026-08-26: all spawn sites run 'xcrun devicectl ...', Apple's own synchronous CLI that talks to the system coredeviced daemon over XPC rather than forking its own children. A code comment (~lines 149-152) shows the author deliberately chose the subcommand that does NOT hold a live tunnel/child open, specifically to avoid this class of risk

verified 2026-08-26: delegates its device spawns into devicectl.ts (same non-forking xcrun reasoning); its own long-lived resource is a keepalive timer, not a subprocess, and that timer already has a correct stop() wired to SIGINT/SIGTERM/exit in the daemon entrypoint (index.ts)

verified 2026-08-26: execFileSync(bin, args, {timeout:120000}) shells out to the already-resolved browse CLI binary -- a thin synchronous HTTP-round-trip client, not an OS-level Chromium spawn. The real browser-server spawn logic lives entirely in browse/src/cli.ts (already tracked as a separate debt site), which spawns detached+unref'd specifically so it survives this client's own timeout

verified 2026-08-26: QLOG_BIN is hardcoded to the sibling script rig-question-log one line before the spawnSync call, not read from caller/deployment environment anywhere else in the repo -- corrects the prior 'externally configured' description. rig-question-log is a plain bash script that does pure file I/O with zero spawn/exec/fork calls of its own

verified 2026-08-26: PREF_BIN is likewise hardcoded to the sibling script rig-question-preference one line before use, not externally configurable. That script is plain bash file I/O with zero spawn/exec/fork calls of its own

verified 2026-08-26: spawnSkill() runs Bun.spawn(['bun','run',scriptPath,...]) (a caller-authored skill script, forking-capable) and kills it via a bare proc.kill() on timeout -- same risk shape as the already-debt sites 5-9, but this call uses Bun's own spawn API, not node:child_process. Bun.spawn requires 'detached: true' to setsid() a process group at all, and Bun's Subprocess#kill() does not accept a negative pid (github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/15791) -- the Node-shaped spawn-guarded.js helper as currently scoped has no verified compatibility story for Bun's own spawn primitives. Needs the browse-skill owner to decide: shim through node:child_process (Bun supports it) so the existing helper applies as-is, or design a Bun-native equivalent. This also corrects the prior rationale text, which wrongly described the target as 'a Chromium-launched process' -- it spawns a bun script runner, not Chromium

verified 2026-08-26: spawnXvfb() calls Bun.spawn(['Xvfb', ...]) for the intentional long-lived Xvfb daemon (no 'detached: true' despite an adjacent comment claiming 'Spawn detached' -- a separate implementation defect worth its own note); cleanupXvfb() signals only the direct pid (safeKill, SIGTERM then SIGKILL), no process group. Same Bun-API compatibility gap as browser-skill-commands.ts (no negative-pid kill support in Bun's Subprocess#kill()). Xvfb itself does not typically fork long-lived descendants in normal operation, so blast radius is lower, but this is exactly the ticket's own Category C ('detached daemons with no descendant-cleanup contract') -- needs the browse-skill owner to define Xvfb's own reap contract rather than a blind helper swap, since the daemon's OS-level detachment story is not what the comment claims today

verified 2026-08-26, HIGHEST PRIORITY of the 21 triaged this pass: importCookiesViaCdp() launches a real headless Chromium browser (Bun.spawn, standard multi-process renderer/GPU architecture) directly against the user's actual installed Chrome/Edge profile directory (Windows-only path; the code's own comment says this must be the real profile because ABE keys are path-bound) and kills it with a bare chromeProc.kill() -- leader-pid only, no Windows Job Object. This spawn happens inside an HTTP command handler nested in the already-running browse daemon (cli.ts, already tracked as debt site 10), but that outer daemon's own kill path only ever signals its own leader pid and never reaches this nested Chrome process, so nesting provides no protection today. An orphaned instance holds a lock on the user's real browser profile, which can block their actual Chrome/Edge from launching afterward -- materially worse blast radius than a scratch-profile browser. Needs the browse-skill owner to design the Windows Job Object primitive the ticket's own proposed resolution already calls for (no Windows CI runner exists in this repo to verify it automatically). Four other kill sites in this file -- powershell/security/secret-tool one-shot credential-store probes -- are comparatively low-risk leaf utilities, direct-kill on timeout, minimal realistic fork risk; noted but not the reason for this file's classification
